title: No new κ: BW16 as a unit — window c ≥ 72 puts its ceiling at 0.649× E8's (checked)
body:
**No new κ.** This screens the Barnes–Wall lattice BW16 as a unit, using the screen main already applies to the ADE root systems, K12, Leech and the Niemeier lattices (`research/e8-decoder-floors-and-cold14-notes/ade_screen.py`, #620; #598; #606). BW16 has not been screened before. Its ceiling comes out 35% below E8's.

## Change and mathematical scope

One self-contained package, `research/bw16-unit-screen/`, plus one path-filtered workflow and one `.gitattributes` line. No existing file changes.

- **Lattice.** BW16 = RM(1,4) + 2·RM(3,4) + 4ℤ¹⁶ (Construction D). It is rebuilt from code generators. All 4320 minimal vectors are enumerated: the shapes (±2²) and (±1⁸) are proved to be the only norm-8 vectors. They give 2160 lines.
  - Every line has the same \|⟨x, y⟩\| profile: {0: 855, 2: 1024, 4: 280}.
- **Window.**
  - `data/clique72.json` holds 72 pairwise non-orthogonal lines. A deterministic greedy reproduces it exactly.
  - At the decoder pattern of `format-limits` §C.6 (#446 Theorem A), the clique forces B[K, K] = I, so the window is c ≥ 72. For comparison, E8 has c = 9, and its largest non-orthogonal set is exactly 8, which is also checked.
  - The pattern's natural decoder B₀ has F₂ rank 191, so 72 ≤ c_min ≤ 191.
- **Screen.**
  - The screen uses `ade_screen.py`'s proxy x = c·h/v = 8/15 and #595's certified `skel.X`, imported unchanged.
  - Result: X(s, 16, 1, 8/15) ≤ 3.8923·10⁻³ at every s = 3…39. That is 0.649× E8's bit ceiling (6.0005·10⁻³, reproduced) and below the full-E8 ceiling (5.1598·10⁻³).
- **Break-even.** BW16 loses at every s if and only if c ≥ 63. So the conclusion does not depend on finding the largest clique.
- **Cause of the loss.** It is entirely the copy charge. With free copies, X(3, 16, 1, 0) = 1.96·10⁻², more than 3× E8's ceiling.

**Scope.**
- This is a ranking screen of the same kind as main's ADE, Leech and Niemeier screens. It is not a κ bound.
- Only decoders on the §C.6 pattern are covered. k = 1, and helper cost is not priced (#620 §4). BW16 has 855 orthogonal neighbours per line against E8's 63, which points the same way.

**Duplicates.** Checked against main at `f567884a` and against the titles and bodies of every hub PR through #883: none screens BW16. The Gaussian E8 clique ceilings (#738, #770, #868) concern a different unit.

## Validation

`python3 -B research/bw16-unit-screen/bw16_check.py` uses the standard library only. It prints `PASS_BW16_UNIT_SCREEN (21 checks)` in about 2 min 40 s. It passed on Linux aarch64 with Python 3.12.3 and 3.11.16, against main at `f567884a`. CI runs it on Python 3.11 and 3.14.
